chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about this matter, so he said: 'Repeat it to me.' I said to him: 'I had a slave-girl who did not bear me a child, so I sold her. She bore a child to someone else, and I have a child by another woman. Should I marry my child to her child?' He said: 'Marry the child she had before you [married her].' He means: before you had [a child with her].
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his child to the child of a slave-girl he previously owned if she bore that child to someone else before he bought her?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of a man marrying his son to the daughter of a slave-girl he previously owned, provided the daughter was born by another man before his acquisition of her. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the lineage and marital eligibility of the child are determined by the time of birth relative to the owner's possession, distinguishing between children born during ownership versus those born prior. The narration underscores the flexibility in intra-family marriages within the context of slavery, ensuring that pre-existing familial bonds do not prohibit union once the ownership structure changes.
